newsitem.title: USA: Swingley in front of Iditarod race pack.
newsitem.headline: Swingley in front of Iditarod race pack.

text.p: Montana musher Doug Swingley held an eight-minute lead over defending champion Jeff King late Tuesday as top mushers in the Iditarod Trail Sled Dog Race began a sprint toward the Kuskowkwim River.

Swingley, 1995 champion of the 1,161-mile sled dog race, departed Nikolai, an Athabaskan Indian village 365 miles into the trail, at 3:18 p.m. (7:18 p.m. EST). King, who won the race in 1993 and 1996, was next out of Nikolai.
King, of Denali, Alaska, was followed in the next couple of hours by five other race leaders, including two-time champion Martin Buser, of Big Lake, Alaska.
Buser, the first into Nikolai Tuesday morning and the fastest traveller across the treacherous wind-blown stretch that leads there, said standings this early in the race mean little.

"The lead is totally irrelevant right now," Buser told the Alaska Public Radio Network in an interview in Nikolai. "We're leapfrogging and going back and forth. It's not an important thing to be in the lead or not in the lead."

The Iditarod started Saturday with 53 mushers making a ceremonial run from downtown Anchorage. The race leads to the Bering Sea gold rush town of Nome. In the past two years, Swingley and King won the race in nine days.
At stake in the world's most famous sled-dog race is a total purse of over $400,000, with $50,000 and a new truck going to the winner.

A second musher dropped out of the competition Tuesday. Linda Joy of Willow, Alaka, withdrew after injuring her hand. An injury, from a collision with a tree, had caused her to withdraw from last year's race as well.
